 Leeds United 
 Leeds winger Noah Okafor, speaking to BBC MOTD: "The first goal came after Dom [Calvert-Lewin] gave me a perfect ball. My first touch wasn't perfect so I did a body movement and then found the corner. This is how I trained in the last few weeks. 
 "The second goal I will need to rewatch but I'm extremely happy."
 On the overall performance: "We know our qualities, we have trained a lot and it's a big compliment on the whole team. We have to keep going and working hard.
Dominic [Calvert-Lewin] had chances, normally he would score them, and I told him at half-time that he would score. We're really happy for him."
 On the Leeds fans: "The support from the fans was incredible. The support is unbelievable, it's an amazing club with amazing fans."

 'His talent is bigger than this performance' published at 18:24 GMT 18:24 GMT 
 FT: Tottenham 2-0 Ipswich 
 Tottenham Hotspur 
 Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi to BBC Match of the Day on Luca Williams-Barentt's performance: "He's played very well, but his talent is bigger than this performance. It was the first game and I am very happy, I am very delighted for his performance, but he is a big, big, big talent.
 "The management of the younger talented players is different because you can't take risks to lose their enthusiasm and their positive mentality. But I think Tottenham's dressing room now is a good environment for him.
 "I put [James] Maddison to play very close to him to speak the same language but also to help him and put him in the best conditions to play. To play with freedom, to play with his qualities because his qualities are very big.
 "He's a mature guy. He is smart and understands the situation. He has great behaviour inside the group and the group is good enough to help him stay calm and to play without pressure, because he has to enjoy it on the pitch. He has to work hard but also he has to keep the passion to keep the love of football."
 On team-mate Savio's injury: "I am sorry for Savio because he is a crucial player for us. I hope it's not a big problem for him."

 'Created history' published at 18:23 GMT 18:23 GMT 
 FT: Chelsea 1-4 Leeds 
 Leeds United 
 Leeds manager Daniel Farke, speaking to BBC MOTD: "The last time this club was able to win here was last century. We have created history but it doesn't feel like this. We fully deserved to win this game and it's great for everyone connected with Leeds."
 On the tactics: "We came here to win the game. We spoke the whole week about this and wanted to make this our game where we play on the front foot. We didn't want to allow Chelsea to control the mood. 
 "We need to have good fitness levels and I have smart players who understand how we want to press and play. We have to be more concentrated to execute what we want to do. Desire is second to none and we are competitive in the best league in the world."
 On Noah Okafor: "We missed him a lot and also Dominic [Calvert-Lewin] had a tough period but they are both key players. I was overthinking whether to start Noah after a long time out but it was the right decision. He was key today."

 'Fragile moment' published at 18:20 GMT 18:20 GMT 
 FT: Chelsea 1-4 Leeds 
 Chelsea 
 Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso, speaking to BBC MOTD: "We are disappointed and sad. It was tough to deal with the defeat and we're in a fragile moment. 
 "We have lost a bit of the confidence which we were playing with. It's a delicate moment but we have to go through it together and find solutions. 
 "The first half an hour was good but we conceded the equaliser and weren't too comfortable and lost some momentum. 
We could have done more in the second half but we didn't regain the confidence to have a real go and couldn't push hard enough to score one goal, which would have changed the momentum."
 On what is biggest issue at the moment: "Everything is related. It's the confidence, this fragility at the moment, the demand of the game, the physicality - everything is related."

 By Sam Drury BBC Sport journalist A late Dwight McNeil own goal condemned Crystal Palace to defeat in new manager Thomas Frank's first game in charge as Coventry snatched a crucial win. 
 After four goals came in a fun, feisty and slightly chaotic first-half at the CBS Arena, Palace controlled much of the second but it was the hosts who found the decisive goal.
 Palace failed to deal with Milan van Ewijk's long throw-in, substitute Brandon Thomas-Asante stole in at the back post and while Dean Henderson kept out his header, the ball bobbled in off the unfortunate McNeil.
 While Coventry's fourth Premier League win of the season moves them three points clear of the relegation zone, Palace remain rock bottom following a fifth straight league loss.
 The match was lively from the off and Taiwo Awoniyi put Coventry in front in the fifth minute, finishing smartly from Jack Rudoni's pass after Yann Gboho's backheel on the touchline had created the opening.
 But Palace were level just eight minutes later through Yeremy Pino, who lashed home after Jorgen Strand Larsen had stretched to keep Daichi Kamada's cross in the danger area.
 Frank Lampard's hosts were back in front after half an hour, though, as Rudoni jinked past a couple of challenges in the midfield before clipping a pass to Tatsuhiro Sakamoto.
 The winger controlled the ball on his chest before belting a left-foot shot high into the net from 20 yards.
 Again, Palace responded, though, and Pino's clever outside-of-the-foot pass found Strand Larsen to nod in the equaliser in first-half stoppage time.
 That's how it looked set to stay until Thomas-Asante's late intervention led McNeil to put through his own net.
 Coventry analysis: Rudoni continues to impress 
 Figure caption, Frank Lampard post-match interview: Coventry City 3-2 Crystal Palace
 With so long left in the season, uncertainty still abounds in the Premier League. 
 But with every passing week, it can be said with increasing confidence that Jack Rudoni looks likely to be playing top-flight football next season.
 Coventry will dearly hope that it is with them. That likelihood was only increased by another crucial win over a prospective relegation rival.
 That Rudoni belongs at this level, though, is a certainty.
 The attacking midfielder provided assists for Coventry's first two goals and was the shining light for Lampard's men.
 More than just his ability on the ball - the quick feet and the cultured left boot are clear for all to see - it is the former Huddersfield man's poise that stands out.
 Even in a game as hectic as this, he was able to calmly dictate attacks while moving at his own pace and invariably making the right decisions.
 The longer Rudoni maintains this form, the likelier it is both he and Coventry will be lining up in the Premier League next August.
 Palace analysis: Early reality check for Frank 
 Figure caption, Thomas Frank post-match interview - Coventry 3-2 Crystal Palace
 If Frank was in any doubt about the size of the challenge he faces at Selhurst Park, he will not be now.
 This was not even a poor showing from Palace. Having twice battled back to level, they found a degree of control after half-time.
 However, they failed to create any clear-cut opportunities and at times looked vulnerable on the break.
 A goal and an assist for both Pino and Strand Larsen will help boost confidence at that end of the pitch, while the return of Jean-Philippe Mateta should also offer more of a cutting edge.
 Defensively, though, Frank will be concerned by the ease with which Coventry were able to create big chances.
 There may not have been a torrent of chances conceded but when Palace were exposed, they really were cut wide open - the opening goal a prime example.
 The fact one pass through the middle then sent Awoniyi streaking clear a couple of minutes later, requiring Axel Disasi to get back and clear off the line, was another sign Palace were still getting to grips with Frank's back four after years playing three at the back.
 Leaky at the back and room for improvement going forward. Work to do then for Frank and, with the Eagles still propping up the table, time is of the essence.
